law: To build app extensions for system features, you typically use a different framework or a dedicated set of types instead of this framework.
Host apps use the framework to find and launch available app extensions.
App extensions use this framework to communicate with the host app and support non-UI features.
This type provides the entry point for an app extension, and every app extension must have a concrete type that adopts it.
The protocol provides default implementations of the code required to run the app extension.
An interface you use to declare the content, structure, and behavior of an app extension.
Adopt this protocol in a custom type, and use that type to finalize the XPC connection to the host app.
Use your code to provide the host with the information it needs to communicate with your app extension.
This protocol supports app extensions that don’t offer any custom UI.
If your app extension provides custom UI, instead use the type from .
An interface you use to configure the XPC connection in your app extension.
